chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the one who is unconscious (for) a month, what does he make up of the prayer? He said: 'He makes up all of it, for the matter of the prayer is severe (strict/hard).'

key_terms.الْمَغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: The one who is unconscious or in a coma
key_terms.شَدِيدٌ: Severe / strict / difficult (referring to the obligation)
key_terms.يَقْضِي: He makes up / performs the missed obligation

ai.seo_question: What prayers must a person make up if they were unconscious for a month?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to clarify the fiqh of *gha’ib al-salah* (missed prayers) for those in a prolonged coma. The Imam emphasizes the severity of the prayer obligation by ruling that the individual must perform *qada* (make-up) for every single missed prayer, rather than a representative single prayer, highlighting the strictness (*shadid*) of this divine command.
